deterministic.reason: This report records the exact reviewed PR head.
README and test/cli.test.ts were not updated for the new public command.
The new hunks are formatted. Whole-file checks expose only pre-existing formatting in unrelated src/storage.ts and test/storage.test.ts lines.
33 tests passed on the exact head.

findings.claim: The documented delete command is not dispatched and exits successfully without deleting the response.
findings.evidence: Both dist/survey and bun bin/survey.ts interpret `responses onboarding delete <prefix>` as the parent responses command, print the response list, exit 0, and leave the JSON file unchanged.
findings.layer: CLI parser and nested command dispatch

findings.claim: A corrupt response payload can make deletion escape the selected survey directory.
findings.evidence: A response stored as storage/evil/2026.json with payload timestamp `../target` caused deleteResponse('evil', '../') to unlink storage/target.json. The helper trusts response.timestamp instead of deleting the matched physical file.

findings.claim: The new destructive command is absent from README and from CLI-level regression coverage.
findings.evidence: README has no delete syntax and test/cli.test.ts never parses or executes the documented nested command. The added test calls deleteResponse directly.
findings.layer: public command surface and regression coverage

exemptions.claim: The direct helper deletes a normal response selected by prefix.
exemptions.evidence: The focused storage test passes. This does not cover Commander dispatch or hostile persisted data.

issue_candidates.title: Existing responses show nested route is also unreachable
